event: İdmanocağı SK (having merged with Martıspor and Yıldızspor) is admitted to the Turkish professional leagues, joining the Second League under its own name and colors.
notes: Detail comes from the club's own official history page; pre-merger club chronology varies slightly between sources.

event: Per the club's official history, İdmangücü, Karadenizgücü, Martıspor and Yolspor join forces to form an initial Trabzonspor under red-and-white colors, competing in the Second League in 1966-67.
notes: This 1966 formation is distinct from the definitive 1967 merger (TS-003). Wikipedia dates the club's founding to 2 August 1967; the official club history presents the 1966 İdmangücü-led formation as a precursor.

event: Trabzonspor Kulübü is formally founded through the merger of İdmanocağı and İdmangücü (together with Karadenizgücü and Martıspor), adopting the claret-and-blue (bordo-mavi) colors.
notes: Merger followed a prolonged rivalry between İdmanocağı and İdmangücü; a silent protest march by Trabzon citizens preceded the final agreement at the end of July 1967.

event: First season as merged Trabzonspor: the club enters the Turkish Second League, finishing 6th in the White Group.
Trabzonspor wins the Second League championship and is promoted to the Turkish First League (top flight) for the first time.
Second season in the First League; Trabzonspor reaches the Turkish Cup final as runners-up (1974-75).
notes: Runner-up listing from the club's honours tables; opponent/detail not independently confirmed in this pass.

event: Trabzonspor wins its first Turkish First Football League championship (1975-76), becoming the first club from outside Istanbul to win the Turkish league title and breaking the Galatasaray/Fenerbahçe/Beşiktaş monopoly.
notes: Landmark milestone in Turkish football history: the championship leaves Istanbul for the first time.

event: European Cup second round, first leg: Trabzonspor 1-0 Liverpool at Hüseyin Avni Aker Stadium (penalty goal by Cemil Usta), in Trabzonspor's European debut campaign.
notes: Scorer credited as Cemil Usta (penalty) by Wikipedia and LFChistory's match page; one LFChistory article text attributes the penalty to Ali Kemal and gives minute 65 vs Wikipedia's 62 - scorer/minute treated as a minor disputed detail, the 1-0 result itself is undisputed.

event: European Cup second round, second leg: Liverpool 3-0 Trabzonspor at Anfield; Trabzonspor eliminated 1-3 on aggregate.
Trabzonspor wins its second consecutive league championship (1976-77).
Trabzonspor wins its first Turkish Cup (1977).
notes: Hürriyet Daily News lists cup wins as 1977, 1978, 1984, 1992, 1995, 2003, 2004, 2010, 2020 (nine at that time); Wikipedia honours list season as 1976-77.

event: Trabzonspor wins the Turkish Super Cup (Presidential Cup) for the first time in 1976.
Trabzonspor wins its second Turkish Cup (1977-78), defeating Adana Demirspor 3-0 on aggregate (0-0 away, 3-0 second leg per Turkish Cup records).
notes: Wikipedia Turkish Cup article records the 1977-78 final legs Adana Demirspor 0-0 Trabzonspor and a 3-0 aggregate win for Trabzonspor.

event: European Cup round of 32: Trabzonspor eliminates B 1903 (Denmark) 1-0 at home, loses 0-2 away; eliminated 1-2 on aggregate.
notes: Wikipedia table lists legs 1-0 / 0-2. B 1903 later merged into F.C. Copenhagen (1992).

event: Trabzonspor wins its third league championship (1978-79), the first of three consecutive titles (1978-79, 1979-80, 1980-81).
European Cup round of 32: eliminated by Hajduk Split 0-2 on aggregate (0-1, 0-1).
Trabzonspor wins its fourth league championship (1979-80).
European Cup round of 32: eliminated by Szombierki Bytom (Poland) 2-4 on aggregate (2-1 home, 0-3 away).
Trabzonspor wins its fifth league championship (1980-81), completing a three-peat.
European Cup round of 32: eliminated by Dynamo Kyiv 1-2 on aggregate (1-1 home, 0-1 away).
UEFA Cup round of 64: heavy 0-6 aggregate defeat to 1. FC Kaiserslautern (0-3, 0-3).
Trabzonspor wins its sixth league championship (1983-84) - the last title of the first golden era; six league titles won between 1975-76 and 1983-84.
Trabzonspor wins the Turkish Cup (1983-84), beating Beşiktaş 2-0 after extra time in the final at İzmir Atatürk Stadium (attendance 17,956).
UEFA Cup round of 64: eliminated by Inter Milan 1-2 on aggregate (1-0 home, 0-2 away).
European Cup round of 32: eliminated by Dnipro Dnipropetrovsk 1-3 on aggregate (1-0 home, 0-3 away).
European Cup Winners' Cup: Trabzonspor beats Bray Wanderers (Ireland) 3-1 on aggregate, then wins 1-0 at home against Barcelona before losing 2-7 away; eliminated 3-7 on aggregate in the round of 32.
notes: The 1-0 home win over Barcelona remains one of the club's most famous European results.

event: Trabzonspor wins the Turkish Cup (1991-92, listed as the 1992 cup win).
UEFA Cup run to the round of 16: beats Dinamo Zagreb (4-3 agg) and Lyon (8-4 agg), then loses 1-2 on aggregate to B 1903.
Cup Winners' Cup round of 16: beats TPS Turku (4-2 agg), eliminated by Atlético Madrid (0-2 agg: 0-2 home, 0-0 away).
UEFA Cup: beats Valletta (6-2 agg), eliminated by Cagliari on away goals (2-2 agg: 1-1 home, 0-0 away).
Trabzonspor wins the Turkish Cup (1994-95), defeating Galatasaray 4-2 on aggregate (3-2 away, 1-0 home at Hüseyin Avni Aker).
Süper Lig runners-up (1994-95); the title goes to Beşiktaş. Trabzonspor also wins the Presidential Cup in 1995.
UEFA Cup run to the round of 16: beats Dinamo București (5-4 agg) and Aston Villa on away goals (2-2 agg), then loses 2-4 on aggregate to Lazio (1-2, 1-2).
Cup Winners' Cup: beats Žalgiris Vilnius (3-2 agg), eliminated by Deportivo La Coruña 0-4 on aggregate (0-1 home, 0-3 away).

Title decider at Hüseyin Avni Aker: Trabzonspor, leading the league by one point with three rounds left, takes a 1-0 lead against Fenerbahçe (Abdullah Ercan 18') but loses 1-2 (Oğuz Çetin 55', Aykut Kocaman 82'), surrendering the leadership; Fenerbahçe goes on to win the title and Trabzonspor finishes second with 82 points (then a club record).
notes: A defining trauma of the club's modern history; it escalated the Trabzonspor-Fenerbahçe rivalry. An earlier 1-0 home loss to relegation-battling Vanspor in week 30 had already cut the lead to one point.

event: Süper Lig runners-up (1995-96) with a then-record 82 points (P34 W26 D4 L4, GF 79 GA 24); Şota Arveladze is league top scorer with 25 goals.
UEFA Cup: beats Slovan Bratislava (5-3 agg) and Bodø/Glimt (5-2 agg), eliminated by Schalke 04 in the round of 32 (3-4 agg: 3-3 home, 0-1 away).
UEFA Cup: beats Dundee United (2-1 agg), eliminated by VfL Bochum in the round of 64 (5-6 agg: 2-1 home, 3-5 away).
UEFA Cup second qualifying round: eliminated by Wisła Kraków 2-7 on aggregate (1-2 home, 1-5 away).

UEFA Intertoto Cup: Trabzonspor gets past Perugia in the third round (Wikipedia lists aggregate 4-2 with the away leg marked 1-3 a.e.t./awarded per note 3) and is eliminated by Hamburger SV in the semi-finals (3-6 agg: 2-2 home, 1-4 away).
notes: The Perugia tie's leg scores/aggregate as listed on Wikipedia are internally inconsistent (see note 3 on that page); participation and the HSV semi-final elimination are established, exact Perugia tie arithmetic unverified.

event: Trabzonspor wins the Turkish Cup (2002-03), defeating Gençlerbirliği 3-1 in the final at Antalya Atatürk Stadium.
Trabzonspor wins a second consecutive Turkish Cup (2003-04), defeating Gençlerbirliği 4-0 in the final at the Atatürk Olympic Stadium (attendance 40,000).
Süper Lig runners-up (2003-04), behind Fenerbahçe.
UEFA Cup first round: eliminated by Villarreal 2-3 on aggregate (0-0 home, 2-3 away).

UEFA Champions League qualifying: beats Skonto Riga (4-1 agg), eliminated by Dynamo Kyiv in the third qualifying round (2-3 agg); drops to the UEFA Cup first round and is eliminated by Athletic Bilbao (3-4 agg: 3-2 home, 0-2 away).
Süper Lig runners-up (2004-05), behind Fenerbahçe for the second consecutive season.
UEFA Champions League second qualifying round: eliminated by Anorthosis Famagusta 2-3 on aggregate (1-0 home, 1-3 away).
UEFA Cup: beats APOEL (2-1 agg) with the home leg played behind closed doors after crowd-trouble sanctions, then eliminated by Osasuna on away goals (2-2 agg: 2-2 home, 0-0 away).
UEFA Intertoto Cup: beats Vllaznia Shkodër 10-0 on aggregate (6-0, 4-0), eliminated by Oțelul Galați in the third round (2-4 agg: 1-2, 1-2).
Trabzonspor wins the Turkish Cup (2009-10, listed as the 2010 cup win) - its eighth.
notes: Final opponent/score not independently confirmed in this research pass; the title year is confirmed by multiple honours listings.

event: UEFA Europa League play-off round: eliminated by Toulouse 2-3 on aggregate (1-3 home, 1-0 away).
UEFA Europa League play-off round: eliminated by Liverpool 1-3 on aggregate (1-2 home, 0-1 away).

Trabzonspor finishes level with Fenerbahçe on 82 points but loses the 2010-11 Süper Lig title on the head-to-head tiebreaker (fewer goals in the matches between the two clubs). In the subsequent match-fixing scandal (2011 Turkish sports corruption scandal), TFF bodies found several Fenerbahçe officials involved in attempted match-fixing but did not sanction the club; Trabzonspor campaigned to be declared champions. The Court of Arbitration for Sport dismissed Trabzonspor's appeal on 30 July 2019, ruling no legal provision allowed the second-ranked team to be declared champion.
notes: The sporting outcome (Fenerbahçe officially champion) and the CAS dismissal are established facts; Trabzonspor's claim to the 2010-11 title remains an officially unresolved/disputed matter from the club's perspective. The club's honours table does not count 2010-11 among its 7 championships.

event: UEFA Champions League group stage debut: Trabzonspor, admitted to the group stage by UEFA as league runners-up replacing banned champions Fenerbahçe, beats defending-class Inter Milan 1-0 at the San Siro (Ondřej Čelůstka 76') - one of the greatest results in club history. Earlier that window they had lost to Benfica (1-3 agg) in the CL third qualifying round.
notes: Fenerbahçe was banned by TFF on 24 August 2011 from the 2011-12 UCL amid the match-fixing investigation; UEFA replaced them with Trabzonspor (Wikipedia, Trabzonspor in European football, note 4).

event: Champions League Group B (with Inter Milan, CSKA Moscow, Lille): Trabzonspor finishes third with 7 points (W1 D4 L1, 3-5), unbeaten at home including 1-1 vs Inter (Halil Altıntop 23') and 0-0 vs both CSKA and Lille; drops into the UEFA Europa League round of 32 and loses 2-6 on aggregate to PSV Eindhoven (1-2 home, 1-4 away).
UEFA Europa League play-off round: eliminated by Videoton on penalties (0-0 both legs; 3-5 on penalties).

UEFA Europa League: qualifies through Derry City (7-2 agg), Dinamo Minsk (1-0 agg) and Kukësi (5-1 agg); tops Group J undefeated with 14 points (Apollon Limassol 4-2/2-1, Lazio 3-3/0-0, Legia Warsaw 2-0/2-0); eliminated in the round of 32 by Juventus 0-4 on aggregate (0-2, 0-2).

UEFA Europa League: beats Rostov in the play-off (2-0 agg); finishes second in Group L (Metalist Kharkiv 3-1/2-1, Legia Warsaw 0-1/0-2, Lokeren 2-0/1-1); eliminated in the round of 32 by Napoli 0-5 on aggregate (0-4 home, 0-1 away).
UEFA Europa League qualifying: beats Differdange 03 (3-1 agg), then suffers an upset elimination by FK Rabotnički (1-2 agg: 1-1 a.e.t. home, 0-1 away).

The new Şenol Güneş Sports Complex stadium in Akyazı, Trabzon (capacity approx. 40,980) is inaugurated in a ceremony attended by President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan and the Emir of Qatar Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, followed by a friendly between club legends. The stadium is named after Trabzonspor legend and former national coach Şenol Güneş.
notes: Groundbreaking was 24 November 2013. The club's previous home, Hüseyin Avni Aker Stadium, served until January 2017; exact final-match details at Avni Aker not verified in this pass.

event: First official match at the new stadium: Trabzonspor 4-0 Gaziantepspor, watched by 22,654 spectators; Fabián Castillo scores the stadium's first goal.

Stadium naming rights: Medical Park becomes naming sponsor on 29 January 2017 (five-year deal; reported ~US$25M), the venue operating as Medical Park Arena / Medical Park Stadyumu until 2022 (sponsor name not used in UEFA competitions).
notes: Deal value reported by German Wikipedia; naming sequence (Medical Park Arena 2017, Medical Park Stadyumu 2017-2022) per Turkish Wikipedia.

event: UEFA Europa League: beats Sparta Prague (4-3 agg) and AEK Athens on away goals (3-3 agg: 0-2 away, 3-1 home); finishes 4th in Group C (Getafe 0-1/0-1, Basel 2-2/0-2, Krasnodar 0-2/1-3).
Süper Lig runners-up (2019-20).
Trabzonspor wins its ninth Turkish Cup, shutting out Aytemiz Alanyaspor 2-0 in the final on 29 July 2020.

Abdullah Avcı is appointed head coach (November 2020; Turkish press dates the start of his tenure to 10 November 2020), beginning the rebuild that ends the club's 38-year league title drought 535 days later.
notes: Daily Sabah gives 'November 2020'; ahaber gives 10 November with the 535-day figure to the 2022 title. One ahaber sentence inconsistently prints '10 Kasım 2021' - treated as a typo given the 535-day span and all other sources.

event: UEFA Europa Conference League qualifying: Trabzonspor beats Molde on penalties (4-4 agg: 3-3 home, 1-1 a.e.t. away, 4-3 pens) in the third qualifying round, then loses the play-off to Roma 1-5 on aggregate (1-2 home, 0-3 away).

Trabzonspor wins its seventh Süper Lig title - the first in 38 years - clinching with a 2-2 home draw against Antalyaspor on 30 April 2022 (matchday 35, 77 points), three rounds early and nine points clear of Fenerbahçe. Goals: Andreas Cornelius (3') and Dorukhan Toköz. Abdullah Avcı becomes the third Turkish coach to lead the club to a title after Ahmet Suat Özyazıcı and Özkan Sümer; it is the first title by a non-Istanbul club in 11 seasons.
notes: Massive celebrations in Trabzon and at the stadium; ended a title wait stretching back to 1983-84, with near-misses in 1994-95, 1995-96, 2003-04, 2004-05, 2010-11 and 2019-20.

event: Trabzonspor wins the Turkish Super Cup in 2022 - its tenth Super Cup (1976, 1977, 1978, 1979, 1980, 1983, 1995, 2010, 2020, 2022).
notes: Year list from the club's honours tables; match details not verified in this pass.

event: UEFA Champions League play-off round: eliminated by FC Copenhagen 1-2 on aggregate (0-0 home, 1-2 away). Drops to the UEFA Europa League group stage (Group H): finishes third after beating Ferencváros 1-0 at home (2-3 away), Monaco 4-0 at home (1-3 away) and Red Star Belgrade 2-1 at home (1-2 away); transferred to the Europa Conference League round of 32, eliminated by Basel 1-2 on aggregate (1-0 home, 0-2 away).

Papara signs a five-year stadium naming-rights deal (announced 8 August 2023; reported annual value 1.416 billion TL / ~EUR 47.8M at announcement); from the 2023-24 season the stadium is named Papara Park.
Turkish Cup runners-up (2023-24).
notes: Runner-up listing from honours tables; final opponent/score not verified in this pass.

event: Disappointing Süper Lig season: 7th place (P36 W13 D12 L11, GF 58 GA 45, 51 points).
Turkish Cup runners-up (2024-25).

UEFA Europa League qualifying: beats Ružomberok (3-0 agg), eliminated by Rapid Wien in the third qualifying round (0-3 agg: 0-1 home, 0-2 away). Drops to the UEFA Conference League play-off round and is eliminated by St. Gallen on penalties (1-1 a.e.t. home, 0-0 away; 4-5 pens) - no European group stage in 2024-25.

Strong Süper Lig rebound: 3rd place with 69 points (P34 W20 D9 L5, GF 61 GA 39), qualifying for the 2026-27 UEFA Europa League play-off round. Galatasaray champions (77 pts), Fenerbahçe second (74 pts).
Trabzonspor wins its tenth Turkish Cup, defeating TÜMOSAN Konyaspor 2-1 in the Ziraat Türkiye Kupası final held in Antalya.
notes: Result and opponent (2-1 vs Konyaspor, 10th cup) confirmed by four independent outlets; exact match date read as 22 May 2026 from Sabah's dateline (DHA posted 23.05.2026 01:21; a ministry page is dated 25.05.2026) - date confidence medium.

event: UEFA Europa League play-off round: Trabzonspor loses 0-1 at home (20 August 2026) and 0-4 away at Ferencváros (27 August 2026, finishing with nine men), 0-5 on aggregate, and drops into the UEFA Conference League league phase.
notes: Discrepancy flag: the cached Wikipedia 'Trabzonspor in European football' table lists this tie's aggregate as '5-0' (and leg scores 0-1 / 4-0), which is inconsistent with contemporaneous match reports (Trabzonspor lost 0-5 on aggregate). Match reports preferred; the Wikipedia row appears erroneous or uses winner-perspective notation.

event: Trabzonspor enters the 2026-27 UEFA Conference League league phase (qualified as third in Türkiye via the Europa League play-off route; UEFA coefficient ranking 169 at the time of qualification).

Snapshot (research date): Trabzonspor is in the early weeks of the 2026-27 Süper Lig; live-table sources disagree on exact standing (one snapshot shows 10 points from 6 matches). Not a settled fact - standings in flux.
notes: Included only to mark the research cut-off; exact position/points intentionally not asserted.
The club's honours table does not include the disputed 2010-11 season (see TS-053).

Wikipedia Turkish Cup honours row lists 10 win years as 1977, 1978, 1984, 1992, 1995, 2003, 2004, 2010, 2020, 2026 and 'Current champions: Trabzonspor (10th title)'. Note: the Wikipedia article intro text on the Trabzonspor page still says '9 Turkish Cups' (stale, predates the 2025-26 win confirmed by en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025-26_Turkish_Cup); the honour table listing of 10 is authoritative. Runners-up count of 8 includes 2023-24 and 2024-25, though the Wikipedia intro erroneously lists only 7 runners-up (stale).
Honours-table listing; individual match details not verified in this pass.

event: European record overview (per Wikipedia 'Trabzonspor in European football', overall record table as of 20 August 2026): UEFA Champions League/European Cup 10 campaigns (30 matches, 10W 8D 12L, GF25 GA36); UEFA Europa League 11 campaigns (60 matches, 24W 11D 25L, GF70 GA71); UEFA Conference League 3 campaigns (8 matches, 1W 4D 3L, GF7 GA12); Cup Winners' Cup 3 campaigns (12 matches, 4W 4D 4L, GF13 GA18); UEFA Cup 11 campaigns (38 matches, 14W 11D 13L, GF60 GA61); UEFA Intertoto Cup 2 campaigns (8 matches, 3W 1D 4L, GF19 GA12). Grand total: 39 campaigns, 156 matches, 56W 39D 61L (GF194 GA210). Club coefficient: 11,000 (140th in Europe as of November 2026; was 118th in 2024-25). Best European results: 1976 home win vs Liverpool (European Cup); 1990 home win vs Barcelona (Cup Winners' Cup); 1991-92 UEFA Cup round of 16; 2011 away win at Inter Milan (Champions League group); 2013-14 undefeated EL group winners.
notes: Match-level stats (W/D/L, GF/GA, participations) from the Wikipedia overall-record table dated '20 August 2026' (includes 2026-27 Ferencváros playoff legs). Intertoto Cup campaigns (2) are UEFA-sanctioned competitions included separately. Coefficient 11,000 and ranking 140th confirmed via football-coefficient.eu and euroranking.net. The previous dataset cited '118th as of 2024-25' which was stale before the 2026-27 playoff elimination.
